memory_update.text: SPSC should be tracked as a speculative shadow candidate for retail supplier data quality and vendor-compliance infrastructure; survival requires explicit evidence of returns, chargebacks, inventory reconciliation, or vendor-compliance use cases.
LQDT is the cleanest visible small-cap mapping to retail liquidation and returns disposition, but evidence must separate retail returns economics from government and industrial surplus cycles.
RSKD maps to checkout approval-rate optimization and fraud leakage rather than consumer credit directly; track chargeback guarantee economics and merchant GMV retention.
BFH maps to merchant financing and retail conversion infrastructure but is highly exposed to credit-cycle falsification through delinquencies, losses, funding costs, and partner concentration.
SABR remains a contested travel-rail exposure: AI agents and NDC can either disintermediate legacy GDS economics or increase demand for neutral aggregation and servicing rails.
SITE and WSO should be used as contractor-distribution reference anchors for repair/remodel resilience, branch density, and replacement-demand economics rather than as obscure discovery names.
OTEX has plausible EDI/business-network relevance but low purity; next layer should quantify Business Network materiality relative to the broader OpenText portfolio and debt profile.

GXO should remain in the returns/reverse-logistics map only if filings or calls quantify meaningful revenue, wins, or margin contribution from reverse logistics rather than generic forward fulfillment.
Need current market caps, liquidity, analyst coverage, and valuation/pricing checks for all visible candidates before Layer 3 prioritization.
Need source-backed customer dependency mapping to major retailers, ecommerce platforms, travel suppliers, merchants, distributors, and contractors.
Need latest company filings and earnings transcripts to replace candidate-chunk facts with primary-source evidence.

summary: Mapped the visible candidate chunk into ticker-to-node relationships for the Consumer theme. The highest-relevance underfollowed relationships cluster around ecommerce returns economics, retail supplier data networks, reverse logistics/liquidation, ecommerce fraud decisioning, private-label/merchant credit enablement, travel distribution rails, and contractor-distribution exposure to repair/remodel demand. This is research mapping only, not a buy/sell recommendation.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether SPS products explicitly handle return authorizations, chargebacks, vendor compliance around returned goods, item-level inventory reconciliation, or integrations with returns-management platforms.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check latest 10-K/10-Q, product pages, customer case studies, investor presentations, and earnings transcripts for returns, chargebacks, vendor compliance, inventory reconciliation, item data, retailer network scale, and customer retention metrics.
ticker_relationships.node: Retail supplier connectivity: EDI/API networks, item master data, invoices, chargebacks, vendor compliance; adjacent to returns-routing data quality
ticker_relationships.relationship: SPS Commerce is mapped as a speculative shadow beneficiary: if retailers treat returns, vendor chargebacks, inventory reconciliation, and supplier compliance as a data-network problem, SPSC's retail trading-partner network could become an overlooked infrastructure layer behind cleaner ecommerce operations.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether RSCG GMV, take rate, seller concentration, buyer growth, and warehouse capacity utilization improve specifically when ecommerce return volumes rise, versus being diluted by government or industrial surplus cycles.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Segment latest revenue/GMV by retail supply chain group versus government/industrial surplus; verify seller concentration, buyer growth, take rate, warehouse capacity, retail client wins, and management commentary on returns and overstock.
ticker_relationships.node: Returns authorization, reverse logistics, refurbishment, resale, and liquidation marketplaces
ticker_relationships.relationship: Liquidity Services is mapped as a direct underfollowed public-market expression of the returns-disposition and surplus-recovery node. Higher ecommerce returns and overstock complexity can increase demand for buyer networks, auction marketplaces, reverse supply-chain services, and recovery-value optimization.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether repair/upgrade and maintenance sales remain resilient versus new residential construction; track organic daily sales, gross margin, private-label growth, acquisition cadence, and branch productivity.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Review latest 10-Q/10-K and earnings call for end-market mix, maintenance versus construction exposure, organic daily sales, acquisitions, branch count, gross margin, private-label contribution, and contractor customer retention.
ticker_relationships.node: Home repair/remodel contractor supply: landscape products, irrigation, maintenance, outdoor living, and specialty distribution
ticker_relationships.relationship: SiteOne is mapped as a reference distributor for the contractor-density and repair/remodel channel rather than a pure ecommerce or returns play. It helps benchmark how consumer housing repair, outdoor upgrades, and maintenance spending can flow through specialty distribution rather than obvious big-box retailers.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether AI travel agents, NDC/direct-connect adoption, and supplier direct distribution reduce GDS economics or instead increase the need for neutral aggregation, servicing, payments, and compliance rails.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check latest filing and call transcript for bookings, air distribution revenue, hospitality solutions, NDC bookings, airline contract renewals, tech migration costs, debt maturity profile, and commentary on AI travel search or direct connects.
ticker_relationships.node: Travel distribution rails: GDS, airline/hotel inventory connectivity, NDC/direct connect, servicing, payments, and compliance
ticker_relationships.relationship: Sabre is mapped as a controversial reference/underfollowed travel-infrastructure exposure. It is directly tied to whether AI travel agents, NDC adoption, supplier direct distribution, and travel demand shifts bypass legacy GDS economics or increase the need for neutral aggregation, servicing, payments, and compliance rails.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Bread Pay and partner wins are growing faster than legacy private-label balances, and whether credit losses in lower-score private-label accounts are stabilizing.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Review latest credit metrics, net loss rate, delinquency rate, allowance coverage, partner additions/losses, Bread Pay volume, merchant vertical mix, funding costs, and regulatory disclosures.
ticker_relationships.node: Consumer-credit enablement: private-label cards, co-brand cards, installment lending, merchant financing, and retail conversion infrastructure
ticker_relationships.relationship: Bread Financial is mapped as an underfollowed regulated-asset expression of retail financing infrastructure. Its public-market label as a consumer lender may obscure its role in merchant conversion, co-brand/private-label card programs, installment payments, and white-label retail credit servicing.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Net revenue retention, gross merchandise volume covered, chargeback guarantee economics, merchant concentration, and whether fraud-loss pressure rises as merchants loosen approval rules.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check latest 20-F/6-K and earnings materials for GMV, annual recurring revenue or revenue retention equivalents, cohort expansion, chargeback expense, gross margin, merchant concentration, vertical exposure, and travel/retail customer wins.
ticker_relationships.node: Fraud prevention and risk-intelligence layer for ecommerce checkout and consumer payments
ticker_relationships.relationship: Riskified is mapped as an underfollowed fraud-decisioning and approval-rate infrastructure company. If merchants face rising return fraud, payment fraud, chargebacks, or pressure to approve more good customers at checkout, fraud decisioning can become a scarce operational capability.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Track whether replacement HVAC volumes, refrigerant/regulatory product transitions, contractor technology adoption, and acquired distributor integration remain favorable versus new-construction cyclicality.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Use latest filings/calls to benchmark replacement versus new construction exposure, same-store sales, gross margin, contractor technology adoption, branch acquisitions, inventory availability, and regulatory transition demand.
ticker_relationships.node: Home repair/remodel contractor supply: HVAC/R replacement, regulatory transitions, contractor tools, and specialty distribution density
ticker_relationships.relationship: Watsco is mapped as a reference anchor, not an underfollowed target. It provides a public benchmark for contractor-network control, HVAC replacement demand, refrigerant/regulatory product transitions, and service-driven consumer housing repair exposure.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Business Network revenue is growing, defensible, and material enough to matter relative to OpenText's broader portfolio, debt load, and other enterprise software segments.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Segment Business Network revenue/growth/margins from broader OpenText; verify retail/customer mix, e-invoicing or EDI demand, cloud migration, debt burden, and whether management discloses retail supplier-network KPIs.
ticker_relationships.node: Retail supplier connectivity: B2B integration, EDI, business networks, e-invoicing, order/invoice exchange, and trading-partner collaboration
ticker_relationships.relationship: Open Text is mapped as a diversified reference leader where the relevant consumer chokepoint is hidden inside a broader enterprise software portfolio. Its Business Network asset may provide exposure to supplier digitization and trading-partner compliance, but purity is the key question.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Percent of revenue, new business wins, margin profile, and automation intensity tied specifically to reverse logistics rather than forward fulfillment.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check latest annual/quarterly filings and earnings calls for reverse logistics revenue, ecommerce customer wins, automation intensity, contract renewals, margin by activity type, warehouse utilization, and capex tied to returns/refurbishment.
ticker_relationships.node: Contract logistics, ecommerce fulfillment, warehouse automation, and reverse logistics
ticker_relationships.relationship: GXO is mapped as an underfollowed logistics infrastructure exposure to ecommerce fulfillment and reverse logistics. The key relationship is not generic warehousing but whether returns processing, automation, refurbishment, and retailer outsourcing become higher-margin or higher-growth drivers.
